repo.description:
## Summary

An open redirect vulnerability exists in the Coder workspace application proxy. When the subdomain-based application proxy processes an API key exchange, it issues an HTTP 303 redirect to the request's URL path without validating that the path is a safe, same-origin destination.

## Affected Component

`coderd/workspaceapps/proxy.go` - the `handleAPIKeySmuggling` function and related redirect paths in `proxyWorkspaceApp`.

## Details

After consuming an API key parameter from the query string, `handleAPIKeySmuggling` redirects the user to `r.URL.Path` (with remaining query parameters appended) via `http.Redirect`. The `singleSlashMW` middleware in the main `coderd` router normalizes repeated slashes, but only writes the cleaned path to chi's internal `RoutePath` field, leaving `r.URL.Path` unchanged. The enterprise workspace proxy (`wsproxy`) router does not apply any slash-normalization middleware at all.

As a result, an attacker can craft a URL with a path like `//attacker.example.com/...` on a trusted `*.coder.example.com` subdomain. When the redirect fires, Go's `http.Redirect` interprets `//attacker.example.com` as an RFC 3986 network-path reference (scheme-relative URL), causing the browser to navigate to `attacker.example.com` under the current scheme.

A secondary redirect in `proxyWorkspaceApp` that appends `/` to `r.URL.Path` is similarly affected.

## Impact

An attacker who persuades a user to click a crafted link on a trusted Coder workspace application subdomain can redirect the user to an arbitrary external site. This could facilitate phishing attacks that leverage the trusted Coder domain. Exploitation requires user interaction (clicking a link) and that wildcard subdomain application routing is enabled.

No direct code execution, privilege escalation, or data exposure occurs.

## Remediation

Upgrade to a patched version of Coder once available. As a workaround, a reverse proxy or WAF rule in front of Coder can reject or rewrite inbound requests whose path begins with `//`.

The fix should sanitize the redirect target to ensure it resolves to a path-only value with no scheme or host component before passing it to `http.Redirect`. For example, stripping leading duplicate slashes or rejecting any parsed URL with a non-empty `Host` field.

## Patched versions

This issue is fixed in the following releases:

| Release line | Patched version |
| --- | --- |
| 2.36 (main) | [v2.36.0](https://github.com/coder/coder/releases/tag/v2.36.0) |
| 2.35 | [v2.35.0](https://github.com/coder/coder/releases/tag/v2.35.0) |
| 2.34 | [v2.34.8](https://github.com/coder/coder/releases/tag/v2.34.8) |

### Credits

We'd like to thank Anthropic's Security Team (ANT-2026-22456) for independently disclosing this issue!
repo.summary: Open redirect via unsanitized path in workspace app subdomain proxy redirect
